sources: ICMR-NIN 2020 Nutrient Requirements for Indians: TEE = BMR x PAL; BMR from the FAO/WHO/UNU 2004 weight equations reduced 10% because they overestimate Indian adults by 10-12%; PAL 1.40 sedentary (was 1.53), 1.80 moderate, 2.30 heavy; reference man 65 kg 2110/2710/3470 kcal, woman 55 kg 1660/2130/2720
FAO/WHO/UNU 2004 Human energy requirements, table 5.2: BMR kcal/day by sex and age band from body weight
Mifflin-St Jeor 1990 (kept as an alternative equation; ADA 2005 review: most accurate in Western adults, overestimates Asians ~10%)
AHA/ACC/TOS 2013 obesity guideline: 500-750 kcal/day deficit or 1200-1500 (women) / 1500-1800 (men); Helms 2014: <=20% deficit keeps lean mass in trained people
Slater 2019 / Iraki 2019: 10-20% surplus (~250-500 kcal) for muscle gain; beginners need the low end
Morton 2018 (plateau 1.6 g/kg) and the 2025 energy-restriction update (up to 2.2 g/kg preserves lean mass); ICMR 2020 RDA 0.83 g/kg as the floor
Adjusted body weight for protein when BMI is high: weight at the BMI cap plus 25% of the excess (dietetic convention), cap 25 = Asian-Indian obesity threshold (2025 revised definition)
ICMR-NIN 2024 Dietary Guidelines: fibre ~40 g per 2000 kcal, added sugar <= 25 g/day, fat 20-30% of energy
